Selection▾

Selected tiles can be shown as a cluster list or as cluster groups containing hierarchical trees. Tree view keeps clusters separate and orders each container's contents from top to bottom by z-index. Ctrl-click toggles individual tiles; Alt-click toggles a whole cluster as the selection; Ctrl+Alt-click adds or removes whole clusters. On an overlap stack, a normal or Ctrl-click acts on the current layer and then advances to the next layer. Once any tile is selected, Shift-click on any overlap stack advances layers without changing selection, while Ctrl+Shift-click toggles the current layer and keeps that layer current. The active tile is identified in both the Selection pane and the grid.

Overlap warning feedback: When an action is rejected because Overlaps is set to warn, the Overlaps control flashes red to show why the action was blocked. During tile dragging, the dragged ghost and conflicting destination tiles also turn red before drop. A tile that was already overlapped may keep overlapping the same original tile(s), but dragging it over any additional tile is treated as a new Warn conflict.

    Dashboard Layout Studio Help

    Overview

    Dashboard Layout Studio is a visual editor for Hubitat Dashboard v1 layouts. It can add original tiles, edit supported tile configuration, rearrange, resize, duplicate, remove, and reassign tiles, and change supported presentation details through custom CSS. Dashboard creation and advanced Hubitat-specific configuration remain in the native Hubitat interface.

    Interface theme: New installations start in Light mode. Preferences can switch Dashboard Layout Studio between Light and Dark themes, and the saved choice is restored before the interface is displayed. The Reset Settings button restores all saved preferences to their defaults, re-enables notifications dismissed with a don't-show-again option, and leaves hub credentials and the current dashboard layout unchanged.

    New tile workflow: The Add button is its own toolbar group immediately before Info. Click Add, drag the tile rectangle, then complete Tile Configuration. The button changes to Cancel, all other toolbar controls are disabled, and overlap is temporarily allowed until the tile is added or cancelled. See Add Tile for the full workflow.
    Preview dashboards: Preview opens a compact working window that mirrors the DLS preparation checklist and automatically changes to the temporary dashboard when ready. The deep-red Preview Open pill shows when that window owns the shared preview dashboard. See Preview Dashboards for the complete lifecycle and safeguards.
    Dashboard and tile creation limits
    • Dashboard Layout Studio cannot create a new dashboard. The dashboard must first be created in Hubitat.
    • Add Tile supports the native template catalog and the basic parameters exposed by DLS. Advanced or firmware-specific options not recognized by DLS may still require Hubitat's editor.
    • Changing a tile template preserves unknown properties when possible, but incompatible template-specific settings are replaced by the newly selected template configuration.
    Template-property limits
    • Tile Configuration supports common properties such as device, template-specific values, a searchable Hubitat and Material icon chooser, background images, links, refresh intervals, and unit display. Advanced or firmware-specific properties that DLS does not recognize may still require Hubitat's editor.
    • CSS can alter how a tile is displayed, but it does not change the tile's underlying Hubitat template or template configuration.
    • Properties that require the native Hubitat dashboard editor must be changed there, then the dashboard should be reloaded in Dashboard Layout Studio.
    Load & Save

    Opening layouts

    Dashboard Layout Studio can work with layouts that were loaded directly from the hub or with layouts opened from a local file or pasted JSON. In the help text, online and offline describe how the active layout was loaded, not whether the browser or computer is connected to the internet.

    Online mode means the layout was loaded directly from the Hubitat hub. It keeps a hub save target and enables hub-only checks such as device names and selected dashboard devices. When DLS itself is hosted from the hub's /local/ file area, the initial Rendered View capture comes directly from the dashboard being loaded. Later refreshes can use the temporary preview dashboard for unsaved working changes.

    Offline mode means the layout was opened from a file or pasted JSON. Offline layouts can be edited, downloaded, or copied to the clipboard, but they do not have a normal hub save target. When the temporary preview dashboard is enabled and ready, an offline working layout can still be uploaded there solely for Rendered View capture.

    Crash recovery: DLS checkpoints unsaved working layouts in browser-local IndexedDB. After an accidental window close, browser crash, or machine restart, startup lists all recoverable sessions whose dashboards are not currently active in another DLS window. Select a recovery to resume it, load the current hub copy while keeping the recovery, remove it, or ignore the records for now. Reloading the current DLS tab with F5, Ctrl+R, or Cmd+R automatically resumes the exact recovery checkpoint that belonged to that tab, even when other recovery records exist, instead of showing the chooser. Hub-originated recovery reconnects and reloads the dashboard first so the normal save target and hub-change conflict checks are preserved. If a dashboard has a stored recovery when you open it normally, DLS asks whether to resume the unsaved copy, load the hub copy and discard the checkpoint, or load the hub copy while keeping the checkpoint available for later. Within the same browser and DLS origin, a dashboard that is already open in another DLS window remains visible in the dashboard list but is disabled to prevent overlapping recovery records. Preferences can disable recovery, omit undo history, or clear stored recovery data.

    Preview / Launch button: When the temporary preview dashboard is enabled, Preview is the normal short-click action for a hub-loaded dashboard; hold the corner-menu button for Launch Saved. When Preview is disabled in Preferences, this becomes a regular Launch Saved button with no hold menu or Preview action. Holding Shift temporarily makes Launch the default. Preview uses the DLS Temporary Dashboard to show the current working layout without saving over the dashboard being edited. The working window displays the same preparation checklist shown in DLS and opens the temporary dashboard automatically when ready. See Preview Dashboards for status indicators, multi-window locking, direct-open protection, navigation behavior, and cleanup.

    No cloud connection: DLS does not use the Hubitat cloud. Hub load, save, device checks, temporary preview, and Rendered View capture are performed on the local network against the local hub.

    Load & Save

    Connecting to the hub

    Connect To Hub
    Discovers dashboards from the configured Hubitat hub. Layouts loaded this way keep their hub save target, so Save to hub remains available.
    Hub Connection Settings (Gear Icon)
    Shows hub connection settings: hub IP address, dashboard app number, and access token. When the page is hosted from the hub and those fields are blank, Dashboard Layout Studio tries to fill the dashboard app number and token from /hub2/hubData.
    Auto Discover App & Token
    Reads the current hub's /hub2/hubData information and fills the Dashboard app number and access token. Existing values are replaced only after a Dashboard app with both values is found.
    Dashboard list
    After discovery, choose a dashboard to load its layout into the editor. Shift-click the active dashboard in the list to reload that same dashboard directly from the hub after confirmation.
    Opening offline layouts
    Load file

    Loads a JSON file as an offline layout. Changes to layouts loaded offline cannot be saved directly back to the hub.

    Paste dashboard JSON

    Loads pasted JSON as an offline layout. Like file load, this does not create a hub save target.

    Offline layouts can be edited, downloaded, or copied to the clipboard, but they cannot be saved directly to a hub dashboard unless a hub-loaded layout context is already being preserved through the JSON editor. When you connect to the hub from an offline layout, the offline workspace is closed, the grid and undo history are cleared, and unsaved offline changes require confirmation.
    Load & Save

    Saving and preserving hub context

    Saving and preserving hub context
    Save
    Opens save options: Save to hub, Download as file, or Copy to clipboard. Save to hub is available only when the active layout was loaded from the hub. Preferences can skip save-time device checks when you intentionally manage selected dashboard devices yourself.
    Important hub-save distinction

    If you load a layout with the side panel file/paste tools, the tool treats it as offline JSON.

    If you instead load from the hub and then use the JSON editor to replace or edit the layout, the existing hub save target is preserved.

    JSON editor replacement warning: When the entire Full JSON document is replaced in the JSON editor, the editor warns that it is still attached to the online dashboard. Saving afterward will overwrite that same hub dashboard with the replacement layout. Use the side-panel file/paste tools when you want to open JSON as an offline layout instead.
    Preview Dashboards

    Preview versus Launch Saved

    Preview
    Builds the current DLS working layout on the reusable DLS Temporary Dashboard. Unsaved tile, device, CSS, HTML, and supported configuration changes can be shown without overwriting the dashboard being edited.
    Launch Saved
    Opens the dashboard version currently saved on the hub. It does not upload the unsaved working layout.
    Normal click
    When Preview is enabled, Preview is the normal short-click action for a hub-loaded dashboard. When Preview is disabled in Preferences, the control is a regular Launch Saved button.
    Hold menu
    When Preview is enabled, use the corner-menu indicator to choose Launch Saved. When Preview is disabled, there is no hold menu.
    Shift held
    When Preview is enabled, temporarily changes the button label and normal action to Launch; Preview becomes the alternate menu choice until Shift is released. When Preview is disabled, Shift does not change the Launch Saved button.

    The Preview / Launch button is disabled while incompatible placement or CSS-transfer modes are active. The temporary preview dashboard is local to the hub; DLS does not use a cloud preview service.

    Preview Dashboards

    Preview preparation and progress

    Preview opens a compact working window immediately so the browser recognizes it as user-requested. The window uses the same dark-title loading-dialog style and mirrors the preparation checklist shown in DLS.

    1. Prepare preview support files.
    2. Authorize the devices needed by the working layout.
    3. Save the adjusted working layout to the temporary dashboard.
    4. Verify the temporary dashboard URL and open it.

    Pending steps become active and then completed, skipped, or failed as DLS progresses. An animated working indicator confirms that the window is still active. There is no final Open Preview prompt: the working window automatically changes to the prepared temporary dashboard when the checklist completes.

    If preparation fails, the working window changes to a clear error page. Cancelling or aborting preparation closes the working window. When the optional preview-sharing warning is enabled, that warning appears before the working window is created.

    Preview Open indicator: From the time the working window begins preparation until it closes or leaves the temporary dashboard, a deep-red Preview Open pill appears at the end of the upper status indicators in every same-origin DLS window.
    Preview Dashboards

    Temporary dashboard safeguards

    • The temporary dashboard is hidden from the normal DLS dashboard list and is reused for later previews.
    • Preview updates only the temporary dashboard; the active dashboard and its normal Save target are unchanged.
    • Invalid non-exempt device IDs are changed to numeric 0 only in the temporary preview copy so one invalid device does not stop the preview.
    • Valid devices used by the working layout are authorized for the temporary dashboard.
    • Matching external dashboard JSON and Simple CSS Editor files can be copied to temporary preview-only files. Changes made through the preview copies are not written back to the original files.
    • Hubitat navigation is disabled on the temporary dashboard. A full-screen warning blocks direct opening; DLS-authorized Preview windows bypass the warning automatically. A hidden manual recovery gesture is also available if a Preview must be revealed without rebuilding it.
    One shared Preview at a time

    While a Preview is preparing or open, the temporary dashboard is reserved across same-origin DLS windows. Other DLS windows make Launch the default and show Preview as unavailable. Full temporary-dashboard Rendered View refreshes are blocked; a saved-dashboard partial refresh may remain available for unchanged tiles.

    Closing and navigation
    • Closing the Preview window or navigating it away releases the reservation.
    • Using browser Back to return to that temporary dashboard reacquires the reservation when no newer Preview owns it.
    • Loading a different dashboard in DLS closes the owned Preview because it no longer represents the active layout.
    • Closing or navigating away from DLS while its Preview remains open triggers the browser's leave warning; leaving closes the owned Preview window.
    Selecting Tiles

    How tile selection works

    Selecting individual tiles and stacks

    Like the Hubitat native editor, each tile location is defined by the row and column of the tile’s upper-left corner. Dashboard Layout Studio uses that same upper-left-corner location when deciding whether a tile belongs to a row, column, or rectangular selection.

    A tile may extend beyond the selected area because its height and width span additional grid cells. The Selection mode controls whether a tile whose upper-left corner is outside the target—but whose span crosses into it—is included, excluded, or selected by itself as a partial tile.

    Click a tile
    Selects the current layer at that cell, then advances the overlap cursor to the next layer. Repeated clicks cycle through the stack.
    Shift-click tile
    When any tile is already selected and the clicked cell is an overlap stack, advances to the next layer without changing selection. The stack may itself be completely unselected. If no tile is selected, or the clicked tile is not stacked, Shift has no special tile-selection effect and the click behaves normally.
    Ctrl/Cmd-click tile
    Adds or removes the current tile layer from the selection, then advances the overlap cursor to the next layer.
    Ctrl/Cmd+Shift-click tile
    When any tile is already selected and the clicked cell is an overlap stack, toggles the current layer but keeps the overlap cursor and focus on that same layer instead of advancing. If no tile is selected, or the tile is unstacked, Shift has no special effect and the gesture behaves like a normal Ctrl/Cmd-click.
    Alt-click tile
    Toggles the connected tile cluster. If none of that cluster is selected, the cluster becomes the selection. If any tile in it is selected, every tile in that cluster is removed from the selection.
    Ctrl/Cmd+Alt-click tile
    Adds or removes a whole connected cluster without disturbing selections in other clusters. If none of the target cluster is selected, all of it is added; if any tile is selected, all of it is removed.
    Selection pane List / Tree
    List groups selected tiles by cluster. Tree preserves those same separate cluster groups, but presents each cluster hierarchically with containers, nested containers, and tiles ordered by effective z-index from top to bottom. Each row displays its z-index; equal values follow dashboard source order. A partial cluster's Select cluster button appears inside that cluster group.
    Active tile in a multi-selection
    The active tile is outlined with a high-contrast amber marker drawn above all overlapping tiles. Clicking a selected tile in the Selection panel, Ctrl/Cmd-clicking a tile, or selecting a cluster makes that tile active without changing the dashboard z-order.
    Double-click selected tile
    If the tile was already selected before the first click, keeps the complete current selection, makes that tile active, and opens Tile Information for it. A multi-tile selection is not reduced to the double-clicked tile.
    Double-click unselected tile
    Is intentionally processed as two ordinary clicks. It does not open Tile Information. On an overlap stack, the two clicks can advance through two normal selection/layer-cycle steps.
    Selecting areas, rows, and columns
    Drag on grid
    Creates a rectangular selection. The Selection mode option determines which crossing tiles are included.
    Ctrl/Cmd-drag grid
    Adds the rectangular drag selection to the current tile selection.
    Click row/column header
    Selects that row or column as a line selection.
    Drag row/column headers
    Selects a contiguous row or column range.
    Shift-click header
    Extends the row or column selection from the previous header anchor.
    Right-click grid/header
    Opens a context menu for tile, empty cell, row, or column actions.
    Selection mode
    default

    Selects tiles located in the target area by their upper-left row/column.

    incl partial

    Also includes tiles that start outside the target but cross into it.

    excl partial

    Limits the result to tiles fully contained in the target.

    only partial

    Selects only tiles crossing the target boundary; intended for clear-type cleanup work.

    Add Tile

    Place a new tile

    1. Click the standalone Add button immediately before Info.
    2. Add changes to Cancel, all other toolbar buttons are disabled, and the pointer changes for placement.
    3. Drag across grid cells to define the tile's row, column, width, and height. Click and release in one cell to create a 1 × 1 placement.
    4. Release the mouse to open Tile Configuration.
    5. Choose the source, template, device or variable, and applicable options, then click Add Tile.
    Overlap behavior: Add Tile temporarily treats Overlaps as Allow. Existing tiles are not pushed, moved, or resized. The previous Overlaps setting is restored after Add Tile or Cancel.

    The placement is not committed until Add Tile is pressed. Cancel, Esc, or the toolbar Cancel button removes the pending placement and creates no tile. Placement can be changed afterward with the normal move and resize tools.

    Adding a tile creates one Undo checkpoint, selects the new tile, refreshes Simple View, and marks Rendered View as needing refresh. It does not immediately save to the hub; use the normal Save command when ready.

    Add Tile

    Choose source, template, and device

    Device
    Creates a normal device-backed tile. The template list combines the hub's current template names with DLS's complete fallback catalog, including Color Bulb and other native templates.
    Hub Variable
    Shows native Hub Variables using Hubitat's global-variable tile template. Use Dashboard variables to show only variables already assigned to this dashboard, or All hub variables to choose from the hub's complete variable inventory.
    Static or System
    Provides templates that do not use a normal physical-device assignment, such as Text, Link, Image, Video, Dashboard Link, Clock, Mode, and HSM.
    Dashboard devices
    Shows only devices already selected for the active dashboard.
    All hub devices
    Shows the complete hub device inventory. A device not selected for this dashboard is identified in the list; applying the configuration adds and verifies that device before the tile is committed.
    Dashboard variables / All hub variables
    Filters Hub Variable choices the same way as devices. Choosing a Hub Variable that is not assigned to the dashboard adds and verifies it before the tile is committed.
    Offline device ID
    Offline layouts use a numeric Device ID field because the hub inventory and selected-device list cannot be verified.
    Template-specific options

    The lower section changes with the chosen template. It can show Attribute, button number and command, target dashboard, text, URL, link name, image refresh interval, thermostat step, unit display, background image, or another template-specific value.

    Attribute tiles: After a device is selected, DLS requests both standard and custom device attributes. Custom values supplied by the device, such as iframeLauncher, appear in the Attribute list when the hub returns them.
    Custom icon: Choose icon opens a searchable visual picker with All, Hubitat, and Material filters. Use Default removes the custom icon and restores the template's normal icon.
    Add Tile

    Edit tile configuration later

    Open Tile Information and choose Edit tile configuration…. The same form used by Add Tile is reused for an existing tile.

    • The tile's row, column, width, and height remain unchanged.
    • Changing the device can add an unselected hub device to the dashboard's selected-device list.
    • Changing to Attribute reloads the selected device's current standard and custom attributes.
    • Changing the template preserves unknown tile properties when possible while replacing incompatible template-specific settings.
    • Applying the configuration creates one Undo checkpoint, refreshes Simple View, and marks Rendered View as stale.
    Fast access: Double-click a tile that was already selected to open Tile Information without resetting the rest of the selection. Double-clicking an unselected tile remains two normal clicks and does not open Tile Information.
    Toolbar Buttons

    Selection and tile actions

    How the toolbar is organized

    The top row begins with the standalone Add group immediately before Info. Add does not operate on the current selection; it starts the drag-to-create workflow and becomes Cancel until the workflow ends.

    The following top-row group contains selection actions such as Info, Insert, Delete, Clear, Move To, Copy To, Copy CSS, and Resize. The next group contains whole-layout actions such as Select, Trim, Spacing, Enl/Rdc, and Grid.

    A full down arrow means the button always opens a menu. A small corner marker means the button has a normal click action and alternate hold or Shift-click choices.

    Select first, then act. Selection actions use the current tile, row, column, or rectangular selection; whole-layout actions operate across the dashboard layout.
    Add, selection, and structural actions
    Add / Cancel
    Starts Add Tile placement. Add changes to Cancel, every other toolbar button is disabled, and Overlaps is temporarily treated as Allow. Drag the new tile rectangle and release to open Tile Configuration. Add Tile does not push or move existing tiles. Add Tile or Cancel restores the prior Overlaps setting and normal toolbar state.
    Select
    Selects all tiles in the layout. This is the toolbar equivalent of Ctrl/Cmd+A.
    Info / Reports
    Click Info to show tile id, position, size, device id from the layout JSON, hub device name when available, template details, and tile-scoped custom CSS for the selected tile. Hold the button for the Tile Information and Reports menu. While Shift is held, the button glows yellow, its label changes to Reports, and a normal click opens Reports; releasing Shift restores Info as the default. When no tile is selected, Tile Information remains visible in the menu but is disabled. The scoped CSS section can be edited directly; every saved selector must remain scoped to the current tile. The z-index field uses the same pencil Edit button, Save, and Cancel workflow as the other editable Tile Information fields; saving writes or updates a tile-scoped CSS rule. If an overlapping tile has the same explicit z-index, DLS warns before saving.
    Reports
    Opens from the Info hold menu. Creates printer-friendly Plain, Relationship Tree, Overlap Groups, Nested Groups, or Conflict Groups reports for either the selected tiles or the whole layout. Z-index is available as both a selectable report field and a sort key. Container classification distinguishes top-level containers, nested containers, nested tiles, and overlapping tiles so multi-level containment is labeled correctly in report trees. Reports open in a separate window. The compact Report, Sorting, and Fields tabs provide configurable sorting, selectable columns, common paper sizes, and portrait, landscape, or automatic orientation. Grouped reports can optionally include a proportional thumbnail showing each group’s actual tile footprints and overlaps. Reports are paginated into true paper-sized sheets with a header, footer, and page number on every page. Column headings repeat on every table page. Graphical relationship groups remain together when they fit; oversized groups continue across pages with repeated group headings, fixed readable typography, and connected hierarchy cards rather than page-wide text scaling.
    Insert
    For row/column selections, inserts rows or columns before the selected line range and shifts affected tiles. With incl partial, tiles that start before the inserted line but cross into the selected range move with the selected tiles.
    Delete
    Deletes selected rows/columns and shifts later tiles to close the gap. For tile selections, use Clear to remove without shifting.
    Clear
    Removes selected tiles or tiles in the selected area without shifting other tiles.
    Placement and clipboard actions
    Move to
    Starts a placement operation. Click a destination cell or compatible row/column header to move the selection.
    Copy to
    Starts a placement operation that duplicates the selection to a clicked destination. Hold the button for Copy to Other Window, or use Ctrl+Alt+C. The other-window option and modifier behavior remain disabled until at least one other same-origin DLS window is detected.
    Cut / Copy / Paste
    Uses an internal tile buffer. Cut keeps tiles visible until the first paste, which behaves as a move; later pastes create copies.
    Toolbar Buttons

    Layout and editor controls

    Layout sizing and spacing actions
    Trim
    Whole-layout action that removes blank space above and/or left of the current layout. Hold the button for top-only or left-only choices.
    Copy CSS / Paste CSS
    Select exactly one tile and click Copy CSS to capture its tile-scoped editable and imported CSS. Hold Copy CSS for local or other-window copy; Ctrl+Alt+Shift+C copies CSS to every open same-origin DLS window. Other-window CSS copying remains disabled until at least one other same-origin DLS window is detected. The button changes to Paste CSS but remains visibly disabled until at least one destination tile other than the source is selected. Once a valid destination is selected, Paste CSS turns yellow and Resize changes to a red Cancel button. While CSS paste mode is active, every other interface button—including Preview / Launch and Rendered View refresh—is disabled; tiles can still be selected. Select one or more other destination tiles; pasted selectors are retargeted separately to every destination. Paste - Preserve keeps existing conflicting declarations, Paste - Overwrite lets pasted declarations replace local conflicts, Paste - Replace All removes all editable CSS scoped to each destination before pasting, and Paste - Add All appends every pasted rule even when conflicts or duplicates result. Choose a paste mode to complete the operation, or click Cancel to return to Copy CSS. Imported destination rules remain read-only.
    Resize
    Selection-action button that sets selected tiles to an exact height and width. Options can preserve spacing between resized tiles and/or push the surrounding layout out of the way. When Overlaps is set to push, or Shift is held, the Resize button glows and the dialog opens with Preserve spacing between resized tiles and Push layout to make room enabled.
    Spacing
    Opens a dialog with all spacing actions: Set all, Set rows only, Set columns only, Unstack and Set All, Inc/Dec all, Inc/Dec rows only, and Inc/Dec columns only.
    Enl/Rdc
    Opens the Enlarge / Reduce dialog for enlarging or reducing the entire layout by row and column amounts. Positive rows/columns enlarge tiles; negative rows/columns reduce them. This is equivalent to selecting all tiles and dragging the lower-right resize handle.
    Unstack and Set All
    Set-menu option that is enabled only when tiles overlap. It breaks overlap stacks apart and sets spacing between individual tiles.
    Spacing value
    In the Spacing dialog, positive values increase spacing, negative values decrease spacing, and zero disables Inc/Dec while still allowing Set actions.
    History, views, Expert, and Save
    Undo / Redo / Undo All
    Step backward, step forward, or restore the layout to the state it had when first loaded. Undo All follows undo history and remains disabled when there is no undo checkpoint. For hub-loaded layouts, Undo All restores the hub-equivalent state and refreshes Rendered View instead of disabling it. Shift-click Undo All reloads the current dashboard from the hub when the layout originated from the hub and Undo All is enabled; otherwise it performs the normal Undo All action.
    Preview / Launch
    Click Preview to build the current working layout on the DLS Temporary Dashboard. The working window immediately shows a compact progress checklist and opens the prepared dashboard automatically when ready. Hold the corner menu for Launch Saved. While Shift is held, Launch becomes the normal click and Preview moves to the menu. While a Preview is building or open, the upper bar shows a deep-red Preview Open pill, Launch becomes the default, and another Preview cannot be started.
    Rendered View engine
    Preferences can choose the Rendered View startup engine: Style Copy clones rendered tile HTML and computed styles, Image Snapshot uses image-style tile snapshots and keeps styled HTML for icon-font tiles when the image converter cannot preserve dashboard icons, Compatibility Mode starts with the mobile-compatible hidden dashboard frame, and Simple View Only disables Rendered View. By default, DLS creates or reuses an internal dashboard named DLS Temporary Dashboard. When a dashboard is first loaded from the hub, DLS captures rendered tiles directly from that loaded dashboard and does not update the temporary dashboard. For later manual refreshes, DLS checks the current hub device inventory, changes any non-exempt tile device ID that does not exist on the hub to numeric 0 in the temporary preview copy only, authorizes the remaining valid devices used by the current working layout, prepares preview-only File Manager copies of matching dashboard JSON and Simple CSS Editor CSS files when present, saves the adjusted layout only to the temporary dashboard, and captures rendered tiles there without changing the active dashboard or its save target. Simple CSS preview imports are redirected to DLS_Temporary_Dashboard.css. When DLS finds a matching dashboard CSS import and JSON settings file, it creates temporary copies. If it also finds an attribute tile whose templateExtra is iFrameLauncher or a tile whose device maps to Simple CSS Editor, the preview warning identifies Simple CSS Editor specifically; otherwise it reports probable external-editor files. The warning is shown only when the Preview launch option is used. It appears in the rendered preview window with an OK button and a Don't warn me again checkbox. While that Preview window remains open, the temporary dashboard is reserved across all open DLS windows. Full unsaved Rendered View refreshes and additional previews are blocked; when the saved dashboard can still supply unchanged tiles, the refresh control turns yellow and performs a partial saved-dashboard refresh, leaving changed tiles in Simple View. Otherwise the refresh control turns red until Preview closes. Changes made through a preview editor tile remain in the temporary JSON/CSS copies and are not saved back to the current dashboard's actual files when the preview window is closed. The temporary dashboard is hidden from the normal dashboard list and remains on the hub for reuse. Preview launches force the temporary dashboard setting showNavigation to false so the preview cannot navigate back to the hub. Preview launches also add a full-screen warning tile and preview-only CSS to the temporary dashboard. DLS removes that warning only from the Preview window it opened and then removes the token from the visible URL; opening the temporary dashboard directly in another tab or browser leaves the warning page in place. If Use temporary preview dashboard is disabled or the temporary dashboard is unavailable, DLS uses the original dashboard-rendering workflow and retains the existing warnings when unsaved tile content, device, CSS, HTML, JS, or other render-affecting changes would not appear in the capture.
    Expert
    Opens the Layout JSON Editor for direct JSON and custom-field edits, formatting, loading a file into the editor, copying, downloading, device review, and applying changes.
    Save
    Choose hub save, file download, or clipboard copy.
    Move, Copy & Spacing

    Move, copy, paste, and overlaps

    Placement operations

    Move to, Copy to, and Paste put the editor into a pending placement mode. The active operation becomes a red Cancel button, and every other interface button—including Preview / Launch and Rendered View refresh—is disabled until the placement is completed or cancelled.

    1. Choose Move to, Copy to, or Paste.
    2. Click the destination grid cell.
    3. Use Escape to cancel the pending operation.
    Push behavior

    Push is available for a single tile or a single connected cluster. It is disabled for disconnected multi-cluster selections or buffers.

    When push is used, tiles to the right and/or below the destination are moved enough to make room.

    Overlap handling and CSS duplication
    Overlaps: warn
    Blocks operations that would overlap existing tiles.
    Overlaps: allow
    Allows the operation even if resulting tiles overlap.
    Overlaps: skip
    Skips conflicting copied/moved tiles when possible.
    Overlaps: push
    Moves affected tiles to make room, using the Push buf value as an added gap.
    Dup CSS
    When copying tiles, duplicates tile-scoped custom CSS for the new tile ids.
    Move, Copy & Spacing

    Spacing and direct manipulation

    Spacing and unstacking

    Spacing Set normally treats touching or overlapping tiles as connected clusters, so spacing is adjusted between clusters without breaking them apart.

    Unstack and Set All is available only when the layout has actual overlapping tiles. It treats every tile as its own unit, moves tiles as needed, and sets the requested spacing while removing overlaps.

    This is the GUI equivalent of using spacing set with overlap removal for all tiles.

    Dragging and resizing
    Move by dragging

    Drag selected tiles directly on the grid to move them. If the dragged tile is already overlapped with another tile, Overlaps is temporarily treated as Allow for that drag so the tile can be moved while remaining overlapped. The previous Overlaps setting is restored when the mouse button is released.

    Resize by dragging

    Drag the resize handle at the bottom-right of a selected tile to resize the selection.

    Mouse-resize behavior

    Mouse resizing grows from the upper-left corner and adjusts neighboring selected tiles to avoid growing over each other.

    Exact size

    The Resize dialog does the same kind of spacing-aware resize, but uses an exact height and width entered by the user.

    The Enl/Rdc (Enlarge / Reduce) dialog applies that same resize-drag behavior to the full layout by treating every tile as selected and applying row/column deltas.

    Grid settings and editor grid view

    The Grid dialog changes the dashboard grid metadata and cell sizes. The current grid summary and editable grid values stay visible at the top of the dialog while the lower area is organized into tabs. The grid change mode is shown in the main Grid Settings box and offers two choices: Change grid only and Preserve layout. Use the question-mark icon next to the Grid change mode title to compare the modes. Change grid only keeps tile coordinates untouched. Preserve layout is experimental and changes tile positions and spans to keep the dashboard as close as possible to its current visual geometry. Because Hubitat tile coordinates and spans are whole numbers, DLS warns when an enlarged grid cannot preserve the current geometry exactly; when Preserve layout is selected, Column Size and Row Size are constrained so no existing tile would have to shrink below 1×1. Preserve layout uses a relationship-first scale pass: connected, nested, and overlapped tiles are scaled with shared rounded grid lines; positive margins and empty-cell gaps remain visible; and container/background tiles grow only as needed so nested or overlay tiles stay inside and aligned. The Recommended tab is enabled only when Preserve layout is selected and scores preservation-friendly Column Size / Row Size / Grid Gap combinations for the current layout. It evaluates columns and rows independently, so dashboards with different column and row sizes still get useful sweet-spot recommendations. The Auto Fit tab calculates Column Size / Row Size / Grid Gap values for a target screen and includes expanded presets for common PCs, Macs, Fire tablets, kiosk/wall displays, tablets, phones, plus a remembered custom size. Fire and kiosk presets use full-screen display dimensions for wall-dashboard use, including Fully Kiosk Browser setups. The Statistics tab compares current and new dashboard size side by side and lists warnings. The CSS Issues tab is enabled only when Preserve layout is selected and issues are detected; issues are grouped by change type, such as font/icon sizes or padding/fixed-size CSS. Each group has one Fix checkbox and lists the matching CSS declarations plus the proposed scaled value, so users can apply font fixes while leaving padding or positioning CSS unchanged. Toolbar buttons use two menu indicators: a full down arrow means the button always opens a menu, while a small corner marker means the button has a normal click action plus hold/Shift-click alternates. The Grid toolbar button uses the full arrow and opens a dropdown with Edit and Trim. Edit opens this Grid Settings dialog; Trim immediately sets the declared Grid Columns/Rows to the current used layout area. The toolbar rows are balanced so the second-row settings group is widened only enough to match the first row after the Grid dropdown was added. The dialog footer includes Reset to Current, which restores the dialog fields to the current dashboard grid values. DLS always preserves dashboard row/column aspect ratio and shows grid gaps by default; Preferences includes a Don't show grid gap option for a tighter editing view and a grouped Auto-size dashboard bounds setting with a Bounds buffer that grows or shrinks declared rows/columns to the used layout plus optional padding. While automatic bounds sizing is enabled, Grid Columns and Grid Rows are visibly disabled in Grid Settings and a Use manual bounds button disables the preference so those values can be edited; Column Size, Row Size, and Grid Gap remain available. The Grid Zoom control in the lower bar provides a slider, an Actual button, and a Fit button. Dashboards load in Fit view by default so the whole used layout is visible. Actual jumps to the dashboard cell size and gap regardless of fit. Fit zooms the used layout into the editor area without shrinking displayed row/column cells below 3px. When zoomed out, DLS keeps drawing enough rows and columns to fill the editor viewport so the blank canvas is not mistaken for a layout boundary. Applying grid-size changes switches the editor to Actual view so the new dashboard cell sizes can be inspected immediately. The displayed grid size appears at the lower right after the legend. Dashboards with Column Size or Row Size set to 0 are treated as dynamic Auto-sized dashboards. DLS simulates only the dynamic axis: Column Size 0 uses the Auto Fit target width, Row Size 0 uses the Auto Fit target height, and any fixed axis keeps its explicit dashboard size. When a dynamic dashboard is loaded, DLS shows a notice explaining which Auto Fit preset is being used and offers a button to open Grid Settings → Auto Fit; the notice can be suppressed. The lower status area shows the active dynamic preset, and the grid size readout labels dynamic and fixed axes separately. DLS draws a yellow dashed Dynamic target boundary on the grid so 0-sized dashboards, including 0 / 0 / 0 layouts, remain readable. When Grid Gap is 0, DLS writes it as quoted "0" in saved/exported JSON to avoid the Hubitat zero-gap reset issue.

    Move, Copy & Spacing

    Resize selected tiles

    Resize dialog: preserving spacing and growing
    Preserve spacing between resized tiles

    Preserves the original spacing between the selected tiles while their sizes change.

    Push layout to make room

    If the target size is larger than the selected tiles, the layout option is Push layout to make room. It automatically enables Preserve spacing between resized tiles and moves affected surrounding tiles to make room, using the same push buffer and overlap behavior as Move to, Copy to, and Paste.

    Resize dialog: reducing, pulling, and conflicts
    • If the target size is smaller than the selected tiles, the option changes to Pull layout to close gaps.
    • When Pull layout to close gaps is unchecked, unselected tiles do not move; only the selected tiles resize, though Preserve spacing between resized tiles can still move selected tiles relative to each other to preserve their internal gaps.
    • When Pull layout to close gaps is checked, every row/column band freed by the shrink is removed from downstream tiles, so the collapse continues through the full layout rather than stopping at the first nearby row or column.
    • When multiple selected tiles form one adjacent cluster with no unselected tiles between them, their internal spacing is preserved regardless of gap size, and the surrounding layout is pushed or pulled using the resized cluster's combined outside footprint.
    • If an unselected tile sits between selected tiles, Resize Push/Pull is blocked instead of treating the selection as separate pieces.
    • Without Push/Pull layout, conflicts are handled by the Overlaps setting: warn, allow, or skip.
    • If the entered size enlarges any selected tile and would create overlaps, the Resize dialog shows a live warning.
    • With Overlaps set to allow, the warning indicates that overlaps will be allowed.
    • With Overlaps set to warn, pressing Resize opens a confirmation so the user can cancel or deliberately proceed creating the overlaps.
    Expert & CSS

    Expert tools and applying changes

    JSON editor and field views
    Expert button
    Opens the Layout JSON Editor, which allows direct edits, cut/copy/paste, formatting, downloading, copying, and loading a JSON file into the editor text area. The Copy button copies the visible editor pane as formatted plain text so line breaks and indentation paste correctly into tools such as Notepad.
    custom field views
    The customCSS, customHTML, and customJS buttons switch the editor to only that field. Edits sync back into the full JSON when you switch views, format, copy, download, or apply.
    Tile Devices
    Lists every tile by ID, its grid location and size, any tile-scoped CSS content that may supply an alternate title, and its assigned device or Hub Variable. Online layouts allow both physical-device and native Hub Variable assignments to be changed from the corresponding dropdown; each picker contains only assignments currently selected for the dashboard, plus Unassigned. Native Hub Variable tiles show their variable name instead of being reported as Unassigned. Location and size are shown as row/column followed by size in parentheses. The first choice is Unassigned for blank assignments. Device dropdowns are sorted by device name with the device number shown in parentheses. Offline layouts allow numeric or blank physical device IDs. In online mode, tiles with a nonblank, nonzero device ID that has no matching hub device are treated as unknown-device tiles and highlighted in red, except system, the native global-variable Hub Variable template, navigation, and static templates such as HSM, Mode, Text Tile, Dashboard, Link, Image, HTML, Frame, Blank, Clock, and Date because those device fields are not regular hub-device assignments. The variable-* templates are device-backed and are validated like other physical or virtual devices. Tile-device rows for valid hub devices that are not selected for the dashboard are highlighted in yellow and remain unselected until you explicitly add them in Dashboard Devices. A Preferences option can skip this save-time device validation while leaving the editor review tools available. Show Invalid and Unassign Invalid are online-only tools. Unassign Invalid clears every non-exempt tile device assignment whose device ID does not exist on the hub after confirmation.
    Dashboard Devices
    Online only. Manages both physical devices and Hub Variables authorized for the Hubitat dashboard. In-use selected assignments are locked; in-use assignments that are not currently selected are highlighted yellow and remain unchecked until explicitly selected. Assign all, Remove all unused, filters, and Apply All Changes operate on both devices and Hub Variables.
    Applying editor changes

    Apply changes validates and replaces the current working layout. JSON editor commits are normal edits and create an Undo checkpoint before the layout is replaced.

    Custom field-only edits

    If only a customCSS, customHTML, or customJS field view is committed, existing Rendered View captures are kept but marked as not reflecting those manual changes until refreshed.

    Full JSON edits

    Replacing the entire Full JSON document still triggers the hub-target warning and broad Rendered View invalidation. Ordinary manual JSON edits do not use that replacement warning; when the temporary preview dashboard is available, existing Rendered View captures remain available but are marked for refresh.

    If the layout was loaded from the hub, the hub save target is preserved.

    Use the Expert button to open the Layout JSON Editor when you want to replace the layout while preserving hub context. Use side panel Load file/Paste JSON when you want to open an offline layout.
    Expert & CSS

    CSS validation and cleanup

    Validate / Format

    Validates and formats the currently visible editor view. Full JSON is JSON-formatted; customHTML and customJS use very basic formatting and limited sanity checks. In customCSS view, the button opens choices for Validate / Reg Fmt or Validate / Comp Fmt.

    In customCSS view, the format step opens a review dialog when it finds:

    Duplicates

    Duplicate selector/property declarations.

    Conflicts

    Conflicting declarations for the same selector/property.

    Orphans

    Tile rules that reference tiles no longer present.

    Consolidation

    Repeated selector rules that can be combined.

    Conflicts are grouped with value bubbles and the current cascade winner selected automatically. Overlapping tiles with the same explicitly defined z-index appear in a separate category; its default fix preserves the existing stacking order between different z-index levels and uses higher tile IDs to break ties on the same level. Each issue row has a consistent skip checkbox, and the Preserve removed CSS footer option can keep removed duplicates, conflicts, and orphans inactive instead of deleting them.

    CSS cleanup processing and options
    • Duplicate declarations are removed before selector consolidation.
    • Consolidation rewrites repeated selector rules into one rule and does not preserve the original repeated rules.
    • Consolidation rows with unresolved related conflicts are labeled Conflicts Found, unchecked, and disabled. Resolve the related conflicts first, then reopen or reanalyze CSS Cleanup before applying that consolidation.
    • Duplicates and consolidation choices are listed with preselected checkboxes so you can accept or skip each cleanup.
    • Applying selected cleanup to the current working layout creates a normal Undo checkpoint.
    • The cleanup dialog applies only the selected fixes unless Reformat after applying fixes is checked.
    • Validate / Comp Fmt first runs the regular CSS formatter and then applies the same compact one-rule-per-line output, split selector lists, condensed rule bodies, and CLI-like sorting as the customCSS tab compact formatter.
    • When any selector consolidation is applied, all preserved duplicate comments are removed because every duplicate is already represented by a surviving active declaration. This includes comments inside selectors that were already in a single rule and comments preserved by an earlier cleanup run.
    CSS status and tile scope
    CSS status indicator
    Appears when customCSS validation finds conflicts, overlapping explicit z-index conflicts, duplicate declarations, orphaned tile rules, or selector consolidations. Green indicates optional cleanup suggestions, yellow indicates non-critical cleanup items such as orphans or duplicates, and red indicates CSS conflicts that should be reviewed. The cleanup dialog can remove selected items or preserve removed duplicate, conflict, and orphan CSS in inactive form; orphan preservation uses one Removed Orphaned Rules and comments block, and orphaned tile-scoped comments are removed or preserved with the related orphan cleanup. CSS cleanup checks use the merged effective stylesheet, including imported @import rules plus editable customCSS, for conflicts, duplicates, and selector consolidation. Imported conflicts, duplicates, and consolidation candidates are separated from editable customCSS items because imported rules are read-only. Failed @import loads are reported by the External CSS indicator. Imported tile-selector orphans use a separate External CSS Orphans warning so they are not confused with editable customCSS orphans. The External CSS review can copy successfully loaded external rules into editable customCSS and remove the active @import statement; if Simple CSS Editor is detected, DLS warns that the inlined rules will no longer be visible or managed through Simple CSS until the external @import arrangement is restored. Consolidated selector originals are not preserved. Consolidation is blocked whenever related conflicts are found, and those rows show Conflicts Found until the conflicts are resolved.
    Device status indicator
    Appears next to CSS Status in online mode when tile assignments need review. Red indicates a non-exempt physical device ID does not exist on the hub and opens Tile Devices. Yellow indicates a valid physical device or Hub Variable is used by a tile but is not selected for the dashboard and opens Dashboard Devices. Native Hub Variable tiles are validated against the dashboard variable authorization list rather than the physical-device list.
    Tile-scoped CSS
    Rules such as #tile-40, #tile_40, or .tile-40 are treated as tile-scoped CSS for copy/cleanup operations. If customCSS contains @import stylesheets, DLS loads imported tile-scoped rules as read-only external CSS. Imported rules are displayed in the customCSS editor and Tile Info, included in merged CSS conflict, duplicate, and consolidation checks with editable customCSS, and copied into editable customCSS when matching tiles are duplicated. External conflicts are shown separately with options to discard the editable customCSS declaration or accept the conflict. The External CSS Rules indicator appears when imported tile-scoped rules are active. Adding, changing, or removing an @import in the Expert customCSS editor immediately reloads or clears the imported stylesheet layer and reruns CSS validation; a dashboard reload is not required.
    Shortcuts

    Keyboard shortcuts

    Keyboard shortcuts
    Ctrl/Cmd + Z
    Undo.
    Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Z
    Redo.
    Ctrl/Cmd + Y
    Redo.
    Ctrl/Cmd + A
    Select all tiles, when not typing in an input/editor.
    Ctrl/Cmd + C
    Copy selected tiles to the internal buffer.
    Ctrl/Cmd + X
    Cut selected tiles to the internal buffer.
    Ctrl/Cmd + V
    Begin paste from the internal buffer.
    Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + V
    Begin paste with push when the clipboard/buffer is push-eligible.
    Delete / Backspace
    Clear the current selection without shifting other tiles.
    Shift + Delete
    For row/column selections, delete selected lines and shift tiles to close the gap.
    Esc
    Cancel Add Tile placement or Tile Configuration, cancel a pending move/copy/paste, cancel an active resize drag, or close/cancel the open dialog.
    Shift held
    Temporarily switches eligible Move to / Copy to / Paste actions into push mode and opens Resize with Preserve spacing between resized tiles + Push layout to make room enabled. Push-mode buttons glow while active. The Info button also glows yellow, changes its label to Reports, and opens Reports on a normal click. When Preview is enabled, the Preview button changes to Launch; a short click launches the saved dashboard and Preview moves to the hold menu until Shift is released. When Preview is disabled, the regular Launch Saved button is unchanged by Shift.
    Enter
    Submits the PIN prompt when opening a PIN-protected dashboard.
    Shortcuts

    Mouse combinations

    Mouse combinations
    Click tile
    Select the current overlap layer, then advance to the next layer; repeated clicks cycle through the stack.
    Shift-click tile
    With any tile already selected, advance through any overlap stack without changing selection. With no selection or on an unstacked tile, Shift is ignored.
    Ctrl/Cmd-click tile
    Toggle the current overlap layer, then advance to the next layer.
    Ctrl/Cmd+Shift-click tile
    With any tile already selected, toggle the current layer of an overlap stack and keep that layer current; otherwise behave like a normal Ctrl/Cmd-click.
    Alt-click tile
    Toggle the connected cluster as a whole; an untouched cluster becomes the selection, while any selected member causes the whole cluster to be removed.
    Ctrl/Cmd+Alt-click tile
    Add an untouched cluster to the current selection or remove the whole cluster when any of its tiles is already selected.
    Double-click selected tile
    Open Tile Information for that tile while preserving the complete existing selection and making the tile active.
    Double-click unselected tile
    Process the gesture as two ordinary tile clicks. Tile Information does not open; an overlap stack advances according to the normal click-cycle rules.
    Add mode: drag grid
    Define the new tile position and size. Click and release in one cell for a 1 × 1 tile. Releasing opens Tile Configuration; the Add/Cancel button or Esc cancels without creating a tile.
    Drag selected tile
    Move the selected tile or selected group. If Overlaps is set to warn, overlap relationships that already existed when the drag began are permitted so a stacked tile can be repositioned, but touching any additional tile is treated as a new conflict: the drag preview turns red and dropping is rejected. The previous Overlaps setting remains in effect.
    Drag resize handle
    Resize selected tiles from their lower-right edge.
    Drag grid background
    Create a rectangular tile selection.
    Ctrl/Cmd-drag grid
    Add a rectangular selection to the existing selection.
    Click/drag header
    Select one row/column or a contiguous row/column range.
    Shift-click header
    Extend row/column selection from the previous header anchor.
    Right-click grid/header
    Open the context menu.
    Shift-click active dashboard
    Reload the currently active dashboard from the hub from the left dashboard list, after confirmation.
    Shift-click Undo All
    For a hub-originated layout, reload the current dashboard from the hub when Undo All is enabled. For other layouts, perform normal Undo All.
    Press and hold toolbar buttons
    Open alternate options on buttons with a dropdown arrow, including Preview / Launch Saved, push placement, trim direction, spacing scope, and save destination.
    About

    Dashboard Layout Studio

    Dashboard Layout Studio is an independent visual editor for Hubitat Dashboard v1 layouts. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Hubitat, Inc.

    Save to hub

    You can download a backup of the original loaded layout before overwriting.

    Hub connections unavailable

    This page can only connect to your Hubitat hub when it is hosted by the hub itself. Browsers block cross-origin requests due to CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) restrictions, which prevent pages loaded from one location from accessing resources on another.

    To enable hub connections:

    1. Open your Hubitat hub's web interface
    2. Go to Settings → File Manager
    3. Upload this HTML file to the hub
    4. Open the file from the hub (e.g. http://<hub-ip>/local/dashboard-layout-studio.html)

    You can still use this tool offline by loading a dashboard JSON file using Load file… or Paste JSON.

Refresh Rendered View after applying the change; DLS uses the temporary preview dashboard when enabled, or the existing save-first workflow when it is disabled or unavailable.
    
        
    
      
    

      
    
        
    
          
          
          
          
        
    
        
    
          
    Recommended Preserve Sizes
    
          
    DLS scores candidate Column Size / Row Size / Grid Gap combinations for this specific layout. Columns and rows are evaluated independently because they may use different sizes. Use these recommendations when increasing grid size and preserving the layout.

    Auto Fit to Screen
    
          
    
            
    
            
    
            
    
            
    
            
    
          
    
          
    
            
    
            
    
          
    
          
          
    Custom target size and the selected preset are remembered on this browser. Fire and kiosk presets use full-screen display dimensions, which is usually the right target for Fully Kiosk Browser wall dashboards. For dashboards with Column Size or Row Size set to 0, this same target is used to simulate the dynamic dashboard size in the editor.
